Subject: Monthly OKR pulse & KPI dashboard — QBR prep

Team — attaching the September KPI dump + a short readout. This is intended for the QBR on 9/08; please surface any blockers by EOD Thursday so I can fold them into the leadership slide deck. Top-line observations from this morning's snapshot:    

• Latency: p50 across hosted API is flat at 82ms, but p95 increased to 430ms driven by weekend traffic spikes in eu-west.
• Cost: overall token cost is +12% month-over-month; the primary driver looks to be an increase in long context requests from three customers (ACME included).
• Uptime: 99.96% platform-wide; small blip on 8/27 (15m) due to autoscaler thrash — note attached incident timeline.
• Usage: sustained growth in embeddings (24% MoM), model mix shift toward larger models for two customers.

Immediate asks:
1) Markus — can you confirm whether the autoscaler policy change from 8/20 is contributing to the 8/27 blip and whether there's a safe rollback option?
2) Irene — please validate the p95 regression and propose a short mitigation (cache warming / KV prefetch) we can trial during the QBR week.
3) Laura/Finance — need a quick note on whether the cost spike needs a cross-charge or temporary credit for ACME; I put a cost snapshot in the XLS.

Attachments: monthly_kpi_dash_2026-09.pdf (dashboard export), cost-anomaly-snapshot.xlsx (per-customer cost breakdown).

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Ckpi-dashboard-2026-09
HubSpot: HS-23094

Thanks — kim

-- 
Kimberly Park

Kim — quick reply while I'm digging in. Short answers first: I think the autoscaler tweak is a contributor. On 8/20 we relaxed the warm pool TTL to reduce GPU spin costs; that allowed more frequent scale-to-zero behavior when tail traffic drops. The 8/27 window aligns with a traffic trough followed by a sudden burst (customer-side job batch).

Planned action: rollback the TTL change to previous value for the Dedicated pool that handles long-tail requests. I'll prepare a canary rollback for 9/03 (non-peak hours) and post results here. If canary is clean, we can roll the change forward as an emergency mitigation before QBR.

Question for Irene: can we coordinate a brief tracing snapshot during the canary (5–10 min) to validate latency paths and confirm whether it's purely scaling or kernel hot paths?

-Markus

Thanks, Kim and Markus. I pulled the p95 traces for the weekend spike and started a breakdown by region and request type. Preliminary notes:

• The p95 jump in eu-west is mostly inference calls that include long context (>= 8k tokens) and a small fraction of chat sessions with heavy tool-calling.
• KV cache hit-rate dropped 14% during the spike window; looks like a key eviction pattern around 8/26–8/27.

Mitigations I propose before QBR:
1) Cache warming job for top-20 prefixes for ACME and two other customers (run nightly 9/2–9/6).
2) Short-term increase of KV cache size for eu-west Dedicated pool for 72 hours around QBR if rollback doesn't fully restore behavior.
3) Tracing window during Markus's rollback canary (agree 9/03 02:00–03:00 UTC) — I'll enable higher retention slicing for that minute window.

I'll attach the trace summary to the Drive folder after the canary.

—Irene
